account: Today I have followed my appointments: the plaza market walk, lunch at home, office accounts, and now tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage. I arrived just before three. I have a feeling something may be going on without me, but no firm evidence of a secret plan. Townsfolk reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery, which could simply be ordinary baking. The neighbour said the baker told them there was no special occasion today. I tried asking freight about trade, but did not obtain a reply. The secretary investigated my tea invitation because the appointment book omitted the host's address; the neighbour personally supplied it, so that mystery is resolved. The secretary's earlier calls were about that address, not some urgent business. No correspondence or account figures had been supplied. The most notable new business is the builder's report that eight lanterns have been installed in the great hall. The builder requested that I inspect the lighting tomorrow at eighteen hundred, stressing that no accounts or approvals were needed, only my opinion. I approved the time and asked the secretary to record it. This may simply be an ordinary lighting inspection; I cannot establish any other purpose from what I have heard. The builder, secretary, neighbour, and baker have featured in today's conversations, but I have seen nothing proving they are coordinating a hidden event.
